disease: Atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome (CFH-related; complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy; aHUS)

emergence.disease: Atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome (CFH-related; complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy; aHUS)
emergence.summary: Complement factor H (CFH) is the principal FLUID-PHASE and host-surface BRAKE on the ALTERNATIVE complement pathway: it accelerates decay of the C3bBb convertase and is the cofactor for factor-I (CFI) cleavage of C3b. Loss-of-function (most pathogenic aHUS variants cluster in the C-terminal recognition domains SCR19-20, impairing regulation on endothelial surfaces) releases the convertase -> uncontrolled alternative-pathway amplification on microvascular endothelium -> C5b-9 / membrane-attack-complex injury -> thrombotic microangiopathy (microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury). Complement-activation axis UP.
emergence.emergent_axis: alternative-complement-pathway activation on endothelial surfaces (C3 convertase amplification)

grades.perturbation_direction: [F] forced by (role x mechanism); cited biology
grades.perturbation_magnitude: [O] OPEN -- how far the switch moves is runtime/Layer-2, not sequence-derivable

per_gene.note: Factor H is the master negative regulator (BRAKE) of the alternative complement pathway: it accelerates dissociation of the C3bBb convertase (decay-accelerating activity) and is the obligate cofactor for CFI-mediated proteolysis of C3b. Pathogenic aHUS variants are predominantly in the C-terminal short-consensus-repeats SCR19-20 that mediate recognition of host glycan / surface-bound C3b, so the brake fails specifically on self endothelial surfaces -> the convertase amplifies unchecked (loss-of-regulation = a functional loss on the complement-restraint axis).
per_gene.src: Warwicker 1998 Kidney Int 53:836 (CFH in HUS); Caprioli 2006 Blood 108:1267 (CFH/MCP/CFI genotype-phenotype); Noris & Remuzzi 2009 NEJM 361:1676

emergence.firewall: gamma reads promoter switch-threshold STRUCTURE only; perturbation DIRECTION is forced+cited; MAGNITUDE is [O] (runtime/Layer-2, not sequence-derivable).

treatment_A_switch.disease: Atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome (CFH-related; complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy; aHUS)

levers.push_direction: block TERMINAL complement at C5 (no C5 cleavage -> no C5a chemoattractant and no C5b-9 membrane-attack complex), pushing the over-activated complement axis back DOWN toward normal -> the endothelial thrombotic microangiopathy is halted. Acts DOWNSTREAM at C5 and does NOT restore factor-H regulation of the convertase (it bypasses the causal switch defect rather than repairing it); net axis effect RESTRAIN.
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] off-causal-gene DOWNSTREAM terminal-complement blockade; the link from C5 inhibition to the corrected complement axis is complement pharmacology the gamma read does not capture. Approved for aHUS (the manifestation) -- NOT a CFH-targeted agent; degree/duration of benefit, the (boxed) meningococcal-infection risk and its vaccination/prophylaxis management, relapse on withdrawal, and whether/when to treat any individual are clinical decisions asserted nowhere here.
levers.src: Legendre 2013 NEJM 368:2169 (eculizumab in aHUS); Rondeau 2020 Kidney Int 97:1287 (ravulizumab)

levers.push_direction: restore factor-H regulation of the alternative-pathway C3 convertase AT THE CAUSAL SWITCH -- re-impose the brake that the SCR19-20 lesion disables -> convertase amplification held down toward normal; net axis effect RESTRAIN (gene/function-level correction of the causal gene, the DIRECTION the switch forces).
levers.agent_class: factor-H regulatory restoration (CFH protein repletion / gene restoration / mini-FH constructs; investigational, no approved agent)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of restored regulation not derived from sequence; this is the forced switch-level direction, but NO approved factor-H-restoring agent exists -- investigational only (recombinant/mini-FH and CFH gene therapy are preclinical/early).
levers.src: Ferreira 2010 J Immunol 185:5328 (factor H regulation); Hebecker 2013 (mini-FH); plasma exchange/infusion is supportive, not an FH-restoring corrective

falsifiers.claim: CFH loss-of-regulation moves the alternative-complement axis UP (the convertase amplifies unchecked on endothelial surfaces)
falsifiers.falsifier: a CFH SCR19-20 loss-of-function variant that REDUCES alternative-pathway activation / endothelial C5b-9 deposition, or lowers TMA incidence, refutes the axis-UP direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: ex-vivo modified-Ham test / endothelial C5b-9 deposition assay and serum sC5b-9 + C3 consumption, stratified by CFH genotype; aHUS incidence by genotype

falsifiers.claim: terminal-complement (anti-C5) blockade is the CORRECTIVE direction (restrains the over-driven axis) but does NOT restore factor-H regulation
falsifiers.falsifier: if C5 inhibition raised rather than reduced TMA the 'restrain the axis' lever sign is wrong; if an anti-C5 agent were shown to restore factor-H convertase regulation the 'downstream / does-not-repair-the-switch' classification is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: haematologic (platelet/LDH/haemoglobin) and renal TMA response on vs off eculizumab/ravulizumab; sC5b-9 and CFH-dependent convertase-regulation assays before/after
